title: Convert all employee names to uppercase.
shortTitle: Convert all employee names to uppercase
keyPoints: map(String::toUpperCase) applies toUpperCase to each name, producing a new stream of capitalised strings
Strings in Java are immutable, so toUpperCase returns a new String and the original is unchanged
The no-argument toUpperCase uses the default locale, which can produce wrong results for Turkish and similar locales
Use toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT) or Locale.ENGLISH for deterministic cross-region behaviour
Guard against null names before calling toUpperCase to avoid NullPointerException
Method reference String::toUpperCase is an unbound instance-method reference on the stream element

s1_definition.oneliner: `map(String::toUpperCase)` turns every name into its capitalised form, leaving the originals unchanged.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **`map(String::toUpperCase)`** applies the instance method `toUpperCase()` to each string in the stream.
- **Immutability**: `String.toUpperCase()` returns a brand-new string; the original is untouched.
- **Locale sensitivity**: the no-argument form uses the JVM's default locale, which can produce surprising results for Turkish and similar scripts.
- **Null guard**: calling `toUpperCase()` on a null reference throws `NullPointerException`.
- **Method reference type**: `String::toUpperCase` is an unbound instance-method reference on the stream element.
s1_definition.analogy: The HR clerk at the National Bank of India is preparing name badges, and the printer requires all names in capital letters. She retypes each name in capitals on the badge. `map` with toUpperCase is exactly that: taking each name and producing its capitalised version.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Stream<Employee>
  ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Rajesh, Priya, Amit             │
  └─────────────────────────────────┘
       │
       │  .map(Employee::getName)
       ▼
  Stream<String>
  ["Rajesh", "Priya", "Amit"]
       │
       │  .map(String::toUpperCase)
       ▼
  Stream<String>
  ["RAJESH", "PRIYA", "AMIT"]
       │
       │  .collect(toList())
       ▼
  List<String> [RAJESH, PRIYA, AMIT]
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
To convert values I use the map operation, applying the String method `toUpperCase` to each name, which produces a new stream of capitalised strings. Because strings in Java are immutable, `toUpperCase` never changes the original; it returns a brand-new string, so the source list of employees is completely safe and I simply collect the transformed values into a new list.

In my banking project at the National Bank of India this was for printing physical access badges. The badge printer firmware required names in uppercase for the security scanner, but our HR master stores them in normal mixed case. So before sending the batch to the printer I streamed the employees, extracted each name, and mapped it to its uppercase form.

The senior point I always raise is locale. The no-argument `toUpperCase` uses the machine's default locale, which can give surprising results for some languages, so because the bank runs across regions I specify the locale explicitly using `Locale.ROOT`. I also guard against null names before calling the method, because calling `toUpperCase` on a null reference would throw a NullPointerException.

Remember one sentence: `map(String::toUpperCase)` creates a new capitalised string per element without modifying the original, but watch for locale and null traps.
